before.name: Question 1
before.problem:
Let 
$T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}x+y \\ 2y\end{aligned}].$
Which of the following statements are true?

- $T(kv)=kT(v)$ for any real $2\times 1$ column vector $v$ and real scalar $k$
- $T({v}_{1}+{v}_{2})=T({v}_{1})+T({v}_{2})$ for any real $2\times 1$ column vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$
- $T$ is a linear transformation
before.html:
Question 1
?

Let T:[xy]⟶[x+y2y]. Which of the following statements are true?

  1. T(kv)=kT(v) for any real 2×1 column vector v and real scalar k
  2. T(v1+v2)=T(v1)+T(v2) for any real 2×1 column vectors v1 and v2
  3. T is a linear transformation
a
I only
b
I, II, and III
c
I and II only
d
III only
e
II only
Submit

decision.explanation: T is multiplication by the matrix \begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&2\end{pmatrix}. Matrix multiplication preserves scalar multiplication and vector addition, so I and II hold, and T is linear. Thus III also holds.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Let 
$T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}x+y \\ 2y\end{aligned}].$
Which of the following statements are true?

- $T(kv)=kT(v)$ for any real $2\times 1$ column vector $v$ and real scalar $k$
- $T({v}_{1}+{v}_{2})=T({v}_{1})+T({v}_{2})$ for any real $2\times 1$ column vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$
- $T$ is a linear transformation
after.worked_solution:
A linear transformation $T$ satisfies two properties:

$$
\begin{aligned} & T[\begin{aligned}kx \\ ky\end{aligned}]=kT[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}], \\  & T[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} \\ {y}_{1}+{y}_{2}\end{aligned}]=T[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {y}_{1}\end{aligned}]+T[\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

- Checking the first condition, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}T[\begin{aligned}kx \\ ky\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}kx+ky \\ 2(ky)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}k(x+y) \\ k(2y)\end{aligned}] \\  & =k[\begin{aligned}x+y \\ 2y\end{aligned}] \\  & =kT[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}].\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

- Checking the second condition, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}T[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} \\ {y}_{1}+{y}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{y}_{1}+{y}_{2} \\ 2({y}_{1}+{y}_{2})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{y}_{1} \\ 2{y}_{1}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}{x}_{2}+{y}_{2} \\ 2{y}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =T[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {y}_{1}\end{aligned}]+T[\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}].\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\text{T}$ is a linear transformation.

As a result, all three statements are true.

  1. T(kv)=kT(v) for any real 2×1 column vector v and real scalar k
  2. T(v1+v2)=T(v1)+T(v2) for any real 2×1 column vectors v1 and v2
  3. T is a linear transformation
a
I only
b
I, II, and III
c
I and II only
d
III only
e
II only
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

A linear transformation T satisfies two properties:

T[kxky]=kT[xy],T[x1+x2y1+y2]=T[x1y1]+T[x2y2].

  • Checking the first condition, we have T[kxky]=[kx+ky2(ky)]=[k(x+y)k(2y)]=k[x+y2y]=kT[xy].✓

  • Checking the second condition, we have T[x1+x2y1+y2]=[x1+x2+y1+y22(y1+y2)]=[x1+y12y1]+[x2+y22y2]=T[x1y1]+T[x2y2].✓

Therefore, T is a linear transformation.

As a result, all three statements are true.

$$
\begin{aligned}T[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} \\ {y}_{1}+{y}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{y}_{1}+{y}_{2} \\ 2({y}_{1}+{y}_{2})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{y}_{1} \\ 2{y}_{1}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}{x}_{2}+{y}_{2} \\ 2{y}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =T[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {y}_{1}\end{aligned}]+T[\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}].\,✓\end{aligned}

Therefore, $\text{T}$ is a linear transformation.

As a result, all three statements are true.

  1. T(kv)=kT(v) for any real 2×1 column vector v and real scalar k

decision.explanation: Swapping coordinates preserves scalar multiplication: T(kx,ky)=(ky,kx)=kT(x,y). It also preserves addition: T(x₁+x₂,y₁+y₂)=(y₁+y₂,x₁+x₂)=T(x₁,y₁)+T(x₂,y₂). Therefore T is linear, and all three statements are true.

after.name: Question 5
after.worked_solution:
First, since ${v}_{1}+{v}_{2}=0,$ we have that 

$$
\begin{aligned}7{v}_{1}+12{v}_{2} & =12{v}_{1}-5{v}_{1}+12{v}_{2} \\  & =12({v}_{1}+{v}_{2})-5{v}_{1} \\  & =12(0)-5{v}_{1} \\  & =-5{v}_{1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
T(7{v}_{1}+12{v}_{2})=T(-5{v}_{1}).
$$

Now, since $T$ is a linear transformation, we have that $T(kv)=kT(v).$ So 

$$
\begin{aligned}T(-5{v}_{1}) & =-5T({v}_{1}) \\  & =-5[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 4 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}15 \\ -20 \\ -10\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In conclusion, $T(7{v}_{1}+12{v}_{2})=[\begin{aligned}15 \\ -20 \\ -10\end{aligned}].$
